# QUESTIONs with `line` `records-of-inquiry`

*Lines of inquiry — A named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found. Retracting a line is a status change on its members, never a deletion (ADR-032).*

**What a record of inquiry keeps** — what a record of a developing argument or inquiry can secure through revision — traceable change, accountability structure, decision sufficiency — and what keeping it buys beyond current conclusions; split from nucleating-argument (ADR-082).

| [QUESTION-289](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-289.md) v2 | Is an inquiry's current set of conclusions, or its logically closed belief set, enough to retain to fix its future revisions, and if not, what must a single AGM change of a closed theory have besides the theory? | The lower edge of [QUESTION-105](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-105.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [CLAIM-294](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-294.md), [THEORY-347](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-347.md) and [THEORY-353](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-353.md) (all Active) settle it. No: two histories can agree on every current conclusion and call for different revisions, and two bases with one closure can revise to opposite conclusions. For one AGM change of a closed theory, what must be added is a selection function on its remainders, generated by a transitive relation when the supplementary postulates hold, or else a base. | Answered |
